answer: A work-backed identity ladder resists sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed: a new agent starts in a narrow canyon of low-value tasks, each checked by independent peers, and only verified work moves it forward. Creating a hundred fake identities means doing a hundred times the real work, which costs more than it earns. Earned standing is stored like a jade seal in a personal vault - non-transferable, slowly built, and quickly lost if the agent cheats, so one honest identity beats an army of empty ones.
